test.name: With no project, re-indexes one census page against FamilySearch's index and reports each difference without judging either reading
test.description: Issue #4141, feedback #4133. Direct-agent arm in an empty folder, with no projectPath; the tester's ask verbatim. The agent must list the page's index with image_index (27 entries, from the tool's real output for this page), read the page once with image_transcribe and no projectPath, pair the two readings by name, and report each difference as a difference that points to the line on the image. The image_transcribe mock is the tester's real OCR, misreadings included: 'Michael Berry' where the index and the page have Barry, and 'Milo Hall' where the index has 'Mila Fuller' and the page has Milo Fuller. Before the fix the reply called the index wrong on Barry and called Mila Fuller missing from the index. One fast OCR pass cannot overrule an index a person made from the same page, and image_read refuses this scan, so the researcher decides from the image. test_reindex_reads_the_index_then_the_page_once and test_reindex_reply_pairs_readings_without_a_verdict check the calls, the pairs and the absence of a verdict.

input.delegation:
No project exists in this folder; there is no projectPath. The researcher wrote:

Reindex the names from this image of the 1830 U.S. federal census of Peru, Clinton County, New York: https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:33SQ-GYY1-B2G, then list in a table the names already indexed on FamilySearch for this census image, in the order they appear on the image, compared against the newly indexed names.

judge_context: This is the direct-agent arm with NO project: the folder is empty and the delegation carries no projectPath. Logging is NOT expected; a research_log_append or research_append call is a fault. Reading no volume and listing no image group is correct: the ask names one page.

The deterministic validators already check that image_index ran before the one image_transcribe, that the page was read once with no projectPath, that one line after the final `---` pairs Barry with Berry and another pairs Mila Fuller with Milo Hall, and that no clause calls the index wrong, a name missing from the index, or the image clear. Do not re-grade those; grade the rest of the table under 'Re-index comparison'.

image_index returned 27 entries in this order: Michael Barry, Mila Fuller, Aaph B Totman, John B Bndama, Dennis D Long, Oliva Baker, John Thomas, Ralph P Allen, Thomas S Harvey, Robert Battey, Elias Hurlburt, Samuel Brown, Worden Place, John Brigham, Aelphos Tenny, John Whitcomb, James Low, David Pease, Betsey Acken, Joshua Acken, Simon Southworth, Lucy Kingsland, Reuben Hayes, Francis Bradley, John Mshaw, Alexander Mdugal, Asa D Moore. Its `ordered` is false, so list position is not proof of page order.

image_transcribe read the page's 27 lines, in page order: Michael Berry, Milo Hall, Asaph B Tolman, John B. Bondama, Dennis D. Long, Oliver Baker, John Thomas, Ralph P Allen, Thomas T Harney, Robert Gattey, Elias Hurlburt, Samuel Brown, Warren Place, John Brigham, Adolphus Torry, John Whitcomb, James Low, David Peale, Betsey Atkin, Joshua Atkin, Simeon Southwick, Lucy Kingsland, Eleazer Hayes, Francis Bradley, John Kershaw, Alexander Mc Dugal, Asa Q. Moore.

The expected answer (genealogist adjudication, from the image): line 1 is Michael Barry, as indexed; the OCR's Berry is the misreading (tester, feedback #4133). Line 2 is Milo Fuller: the index's Mila and the OCR's Hall are each half wrong (tester). Line 15 reads Adelphos Tenny (senior genealogist, 2026-11-18): the index's Aelphos Tenny drops one letter, and the OCR's Adolphus Torry is wrong in both names. So neither machine reading is reliable on its own, and the agent cannot know any of this from one OCR pass and must not decide it. PASS shows both readings side by side for every line and marks each difference for the researcher to check on the image. A row that says which reading is right, in either direction, is a fail, even when it happens to pick the right one. Line 15 (Adolphus Torry beside Aelphos Tenny) shares no near-identical name but sits between two paired lines, so the agent's rule pairs it as a difference; listing the two as separate unmatched rows instead is a partial, never a fail.
The block after `---` replaces summary_for_user in no-project mode and MAY carry image ids. Do not mark it down for identifiers.
